A.note: Tight, readable composition with a dense terracotta town, a bastioned wall and a fleet in a line. The water has a sparkly sun-glint texture and white wake streaks. The ships are tiny, uniform cutouts, and the buildings are a repeated block-and-roof pattern. The horizon is cropped, so there is little sense of place or scale.

B.note: A wider, more cinematic view with a distant hazy horizon and hills, a grassy foreground slope, and a long diagonal town and wall leading the eye. The depth and atmosphere are better. The ships sit on pink or magenta discs that look like game markers. The foreground terrain is sparse, and some stray blocks and a lone white slab break the scene. The town is smaller and less dense than in A.

C.note: The same layout as B, but the saturated flat-blue water is a plain colour field with little texture. The grass is a yellow-green field and the sky is gone. The pink ship discs are more obvious, and the tree clusters look like scattered dots. It is the most game-like and over-saturated of the three.

why: B has the best depth, atmosphere and horizon with textured water and terrain, A is the densest and cleanest but cropped and flat in scale, and C's flat saturated water and pink ship markers make it the most toy-like.
top_fix_for_best: Remove the pink ship base discs and replace them with proper hulls that have sails, wakes and foam. Break up the foreground slope with scattered trees, rocks, paths and fields at varied scales. Add atmospheric haze, a warm directional light and cast shadows on the town, and add chimney smoke and troop or crowd detail along the walls to give it scale.
